subject: Anchor + Accelerator construct for per-token pricing — proposal and questions
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmerobotics.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.g@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Anchor + Accelerator construct for per-token pricing — proposal and questions

Hi Ellen / Samir,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion, attached is a focused proposal that tries to balance Acme's desire for low marginal economics as volume scales while keeping Redwood's revenue visibility (we call it an "Anchor + Accelerator" construct). High level:

- Anchor: a fixed baseline monthly commit (tokens) that guarantees a predictable minimum effective rate.
- Accelerator: a graduated accelerator ladder that slices incremental usage above the anchor into marginal discounts (higher usage -> lower marginal price for the incremental tokens).
- Invoice smoothing / true-up: end-of-quarter true-up where we compare realized usage to anchor and apply a smoothing credit so your monthly billing doesn't spike unexpectedly.

I've included two worked examples (sheet tabs: marginal_example, blended_example) to show the difference between purely blended effective rates versus marginal per-slice pricing. The attachments: RDW-Acme-anchor-accelerator-v1.xlsx and usage-model-scenarios-ACME.csv.

Questions for you:
1) Is Acme comfortable with a firm 3-month anchor (committed minimum) with quarterly true-ups, or do you prefer a rolling monthly anchor?
2) Do you want accelerator breakpoints defined as absolute token counts or as a % of anchor?
3) Any procurement constraints around per-line-item invoicing or preferring a blended single-line invoice?

If it's helpful, we can run your internal usage profile through our model (Drive link below) and produce an expected monthly invoice band under both marginal and blended variants.

Link to model: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRDW-anchor-accelerator-model

Next steps: happy to iterate — propose a quick 30-minute run-through Wednesday or Thursday.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0123

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmerobotics.com>

Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Anchor + Accelerator construct for per-token pricing — proposal and questions

Rafael,

Thanks for the summary and the workbook — useful framing. A couple quick clarifying items from procurement and finance:

- We prefer monthly billing with a single invoice line if possible; multiple line items add reconciliation overhead. Is the blended effective-rate option compatible with that?
- On true-ups: our accounting team dislikes large end-of-quarter credits. Can you explain the smoothing approach — is it a capped credit per month or a one-time true-up?
- On breakpoints: we'd rather see breakpoints as absolute token thresholds (our traffic projection team thinks in token counts).

Also curious on the commercial impact: in your model, how different is the effective rate in year 1 between marginal-sliced accelerators vs blended slab?

We can do Thu 2pm PT for a quick review.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Procurement | Acme Robotics

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmerobotics.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.g@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 08:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Anchor + Accelerator construct for per-token pricing — proposal and questions

Ellen / Samir,

Great questions — short answers up front:
- Blended single-line invoice: absolutely possible. The blended option aggregates the marginal slices into an effective per-token rate for the invoice. We'll still calculate marginal on the back end for fairness and reporting, but the invoice can present a single blended number.
- Smoothing / true-up: we propose a capped monthly smoothing credit (example in sheet: smoothing_policy tab). Mechanically: each month we compute usage vs monthly pro-rata anchor; if usage is below anchor we don't invoice less than the anchor minimum, but we carry the deficit forward and apply a capped smoothing credit in subsequent months so you avoid a single large negative invoice. At quarter end we reconcile any remaining gap with a true-up credit/charge. This reduces month-to-month volatility for you while preserving revenue predictability for us.
- Breakpoints: will use absolute token thresholds per your preference.

Regarding effective-rate deltas: in the model I attached (sheet: comparison_summary) there are scenario rows for low/medium/high growth. Example takeaway: under Acme's medium forecast, marginal-sliced accelerators deliver ~12% lower effective cost in year 1 vs a conservative blended slab (same revenue commitment), but the difference shrinks in year 2 as anchor utilization increases. I'll run one additional scenario that pins breakpoints at absolute counts you provided in the spreadsheet.

For Thu 2pm PT — proposing 30 mins: invite sent (calendar link in Drive). Agenda: walk model, confirm anchor term, confirm invoice format, agree breakpoints.

Action items:
- Rafael: run absolute-breakpoint scenarios and add a blended single-line invoice view (by EOD Thu).
- Ben: assist with legal on minimal invoice wording for the anchor line item.

Thanks — talk soon.
Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Anchor + Accelerator construct for per-token pricing — proposal and questions

Forwarding with quick internal note for transparency.

Rafael / Ben — this looks aligned with our playbook for enterprise hosted API deals. A couple of internal guardrails:
- Keep the accelerator ladder to no more than 4 slices to limit complexity on the billing side.
- Cap the quarterly smoothing credit at 15% of the quarterly anchor value to protect margin.
- Include an easy opt-out to convert to a pure monthly consumption plan after the first 12 months (with a 30-day notice).

If Acme agrees on the above, we can produce a redline and DocuSign packet. Samir / Ellen — we'll prepare a Docusign for signature once you confirm the breakpoints; draft will include blended invoice view + appendix with marginal math for audit.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue | Redwood Inference

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmerobotics.com>

Marissa / Rafael,

Thanks — the guardrails look reasonable. Two quick confirmations from our side:
1) We prefer the 4-slice ladder (absolute token breakpoints) and the quarterly smoothing cap at 15% is acceptable.
2) Please send the blended invoice example and the DocuSign packet; Samir and I will review with finance next week.

We'll confirm final breakpoints by Mon EOD; please expect a short follow-up then.

Regards,
Ellen
